identification_basis: User accepted the photo-based first-pass identification as authoritative for this prototype.

occupants.light: Bright filtered or indirect light; avoid strong direct summer or midday sun.
occupants.root_moisture: Use open bark-based orchid medium. Water thoroughly, drain completely, and water again when nearly dry; do not keep soggy or let roots remain completely dry.

occupants.light: Bright filtered or indirect light; direct sun can bleach or scorch foliage.
occupants.root_moisture: Keep evenly moist during active growth but not waterlogged; reduce watering in winter without allowing prolonged complete dryness.

temperature_f.basis: Conservative operational overlap inferred from the sourced species ranges; stable conditions and avoidance of drafts matter more than an exact point target.

humidity_percent.basis: Phalaenopsis has a sourced 50-80% range; the foliage species consistently require high humidity. Values are an operational shared target, not a universal biological threshold.

shared_environment.light: Bright indirect or filtered light with no strong direct midday sun.
shared_environment.airflow: Provide gentle air movement, especially at high humidity, while avoiding cold or hot drafts.

moisture_zones.requirement: Evenly moist and well drained, never continuously soggy.
moisture_zones.sensor_scope: The single capacitive soil probe should be installed here. Its calibrated index describes this local zone only.

moisture_zones.requirement: Open bark medium that drains freely and becomes nearly dry between thorough waterings.
moisture_zones.sensor_scope: Not represented by the foliage-zone probe; assess orchid roots and bark separately unless a second calibrated probe is added.

interpretation_rules: Never translate generic care guidance directly into the 0-100 soil index before in-pot calibration.
A single soil reading cannot establish the moisture condition of both substrate zones.
If the orchid and foliage roots share one undivided medium, report the incompatible moisture requirements rather than claiming one moisture target is optimal for every occupant.
Treat care ranges as guidance and current sensor measurements as observations; neither alone proves plant health.
